scope: Learning library direct entry, unit detail D1 dispatch consolidation, and intent prefetch

priorProductionObservation.source: Sites Worker logs, successful HTTP 200 requests only

controlledBenchmark.interpretation: The artificial delay exposes D1 dispatch structure and relative wait reduction only; it is not a production latency claim.

statements: authenticated user plus unread notification count
learning source and unit summary JSON aggregation

batchContents: published unit, source, and current-user progress
current-user attempts for questions in the unit
unitDetail.responseAssembly: The four route-data results are assembled after the single batch completes.

prefetch.routeModule: LearningPage uses a retryable shared import promise and starts loading from the application entry point.
prefetch.libraryData: Learning navigation pointer enter, pointer down, or keyboard focus starts a five-minute React Query prefetch.
prefetch.unitDetail: Learning card pointer enter or keyboard focus starts the same query used by the modal, so a successful prefetch is reused on click.

correctnessAndSecurity.identity: Server identity still comes only from platform authenticated-user headers.
correctnessAndSecurity.authorization: Learning progress and attempts remain constrained to the resolved current user in server-side SQL.
correctnessAndSecurity.rateLimit: The per-user per-route rate-limit upsert remains in the same D1 batch and is asserted before the response is returned.
correctnessAndSecurity.publicationBoundary: Only published units under allowed source statuses can be returned.
correctnessAndSecurity.missingUnit: An empty unit result still produces HTTP 404.
correctnessAndSecurity.cacheAuthority: React Query caches server responses but does not become the durable source of truth.

assertions: learning bootstrap uses one D1 batch and three statements for an established user
learning unit detail uses one D1 batch and six statements for an established user
bootstrap and detail payloads retain their expected shapes
direct /learning entry uses one bootstrap HTTP request and hydrates the learning cache
learning navigation intent starts library prefetch
learning card hover starts detail prefetch
opening a prefetched card reuses the cached request

regressionEvidence.typecheck: passed for the full workspace and Sites Worker
regressionEvidence.lint: passed for all changed implementation, test, and benchmark files

deploymentPackagingGuard.initialPublishStatus: failed before the version became live
deploymentPackagingGuard.failure: The repository-root migration history was packaged and attempted to recreate job_source_snapshot_items.
deploymentPackagingGuard.correctedProcedure: preparePackageStage was used before the official Sites packager so repository-root baseline migrations were not overlaid.

limitations: Controlled timings exclude internet latency, browser rendering, asset downloads, and production D1 latency.
The one-dispatch counts describe steady reads for an already provisioned unchanged user; first-ever account provisioning can require additional writes and reads.
Intent prefetch reduces click-to-content wait only when the pointer or keyboard focus arrives before activation and the request completes or advances in time.
No post-deployment production latency percentile is claimed in this manifest.
No schema migration or new index was added because the measured bottleneck was dispatch structure and the relevant unit, question, flashcard, progress, and attempt indexes already exist.
